title: Logos and color

location.series: IBM Logo and Brand Guidelines for Third Parties / copyright 2022

slide_intent: Use the correct optical logo drawing for the background, because a simple color inversion can change perceived bar weight and clarity.
strategic_value: Consistent positive and reversed marks can preserve IBM’s visual integrity across light and dark partner materials.
demonstration: A left explanation and Blue 60 specifications accompany six panels: three dark marks on light backgrounds and three reversed marks on dark backgrounds.
practical_value: Select the supplied positive or reversed mark before pairing it with a background color.

content_islands.name: Version guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the heading and explanation of optical differences in the left column.

content_islands.name: Blue 60 specification
content_islands.spec: Below the copy, list PMS 2132, RGB 15/98/254 and CMYK 80/60/0/0, followed by the design-language link.

content_islands.name: Background comparison
content_islands.spec: Fill the right area with a three-column, two-row array of contrasting logo/background combinations.

ingredient.name: Positive and reversed 8-bar artwork
ingredient.role: Preserve optical weight and recognition on different backgrounds.
ingredient.application: Choose the appropriate supplied version for a light or dark field; use the specified Blue 60 values when applying that color.
ingredient.scope: Copyright 2022 third-party guide. The six background panels are examples, not an exhaustive new palette.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text explains that subtle differences between positive and reversed artwork preserve optical integrity.
reference_purposes.Expression: Six color panels demonstrate IBM’s blue, neutral and reversed logo treatments.
reference_purposes.Application: The page supplies Blue 60 values and examples for choosing the appropriate logo version.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source directs use of the appropriate positive or reversed artwork for the background.
